I recently dined at Azad Pure Veg Restaurant, a place I’ve long anticipated visiting. Years ago, this spot was celebrated for serving the best Vada Pav in Mulund. I used to stop by occasionally for a bite of that delicious snack, and now, it has transformed into a full-fledged restaurant.

Upon entering, I was impressed by the well-maintained ambiance and clever space management. The restaurant offers both air-conditioned and non-AC seating areas, catering to different preferences. The cleanliness and hygiene standards are commendable, which is always a plus for any dining experience.

We ordered a Manchurian starter and sizzlers, and I was pleasantly surprised by the generous portions. Unlike many other places where you find yourself searching for the cooked portion of sizzler, Azad serves a substantial amount of noodles and rice, along with a delightful paneer gravy. They also add a refreshing salad and crispy fries to the plate, making it a hearty meal.

What struck me the most was the overall value for money. The dishes we ordered were both economical and incredibly tasty. If you're weary of overpriced, exotic meals, Azad Pure Veg is a fantastic spot for enjoying traditional food with family or friends.

featured_reviews.name: Punit Teckchandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience was genuinely disappointing enough to deserve one. From the moment we arrived, the overall atmosphere felt unwelcoming and poorly managed. What should have been a relaxing dining experience turned into a frustrating one because of how uncomfortable and disorganized everything felt. The restaurant seemed more focused on managing turnover than actually making customers feel valued.

The food was another major letdown, especially the vegetarian dishes. The quality did not match the prices at all. The dishes lacked flavor, freshness, and any real attention to detail. It honestly felt like the food was prepared without much care or consistency. As someone who appreciates good vegetarian food, this was particularly disappointing because the menu looked far more promising than what was actually served.

What stood out the most, unfortunately, was the service. The staff came across as dismissive and inattentive, and there was very little professionalism in the way customers were handled. Basic requests and concerns did not feel important to them, and there was no genuine effort to create a positive experience. Hospitality is what makes people return to a restaurant, and that was completely missing here.

On top of that, the restaurant also lacked consideration for customer comfort overall. Parking was inconvenient, accessibility for wheelchair users was poor, and the environment did not feel family-friendly. Even dietary restrictions and preferences did not seem to be taken seriously. Altogether, it felt like the restaurant was trying to maximize customers without maintaining the standards and care that people expect when dining out. Sadly, this is not a place I would return to or recommend to others.

Kirti Mahal at Paachrasta, Mulund, is a delightful pure veg restaurant that offers an exceptional dining experience. The restaurant's ambiance is cozy, with separate sections for both AC and non-AC dining. The AC section boasts comfortable lounge seating that ensures a pleasant meal.

The staff is a real asset, providing valuable insights to help customers select the best dishes from the extensive menu. We started with the iconic Wada Sambar, a Kirti Mahal specialty. The sambar is authentic and bursting with flavor, invoking childhood memories of craving this classic dish.

One of the highlights of our visit was the Cheese Pav Bhaji, a true taste extravaganza. It's generously loaded with cheese, creating a mouthwatering delight. Don't forget to order extra pav if you're not a fan of waiting, as this dish is immensely popular.

We also tried the Alu Mutter with Butter Roti, and it didn't disappoint. The gravy was expertly prepared, catering to our taste buds perfectly. Overall, our experience at Kirti Mahal was nothing short of awesome. I would give hygiene 4 as there was water dripping from the roof or else would have rated hygiene 5⭐️. If you're in Mulund and seeking a fantastic veg dining experience, a visit to Kirti Mahal is a must. It promises to be a magnificent culinary journey you won't forget.

featured_reviews.name: Bombay Bhukkad Gang
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vishwa Bharati Veg Restaurant, standing as a symbol of culinary legacy for over 50 years, remains an emblem of timeless taste and unwavering quality. Nestled opposite Mulund station, this gem retains its authentic charm while subtly evolving, much like its shift from wooden to stainless steel seating.

Introduced to this culinary haven by my parents in childhood, revisiting after 33 years revealed an unchanged, delightful essence. The Medu Vada, a hallmark of their menu, still tantalizes the taste buds, accompanied by a delectable sambar that lingers on the palate. The Dal Rice, a simple yet flavorful dish, and the Puri Bhaji, despite a slight saltiness in the bhaji, showcased the restaurant's commitment to maintaining traditional flavors.

The journey of flavors continued with the Dahi Vada, a dish that melted hearts with its exquisite softness and mouthwatering taste, triggering a nostalgic rush reminiscent of cherished childhood memories.

The staff, with their attentive and polite service, added to the overall pleasant experience. Vishwa Bharati Veg Restaurant not only offers delicious food but also carries the warmth of nostalgia, making every visit a reminiscent journey back in time. For those seeking a taste of tradition and culinary heritage, Vishwa Bharati stands as an unwavering beacon of exceptional taste and quality.

Pretty much all the dishes were good. Sichuan chilli paneer, Pita Platter, Mexican Pizza and Khau Suey. Pita platter had way too many dips which go waste as the bread finishes earlier. The dips need to be proportional to the bread.

Khau Suey was stellar. But the waiter did a very sloppy job of preparing the individual Khau Suey bowls with the curry dripping on all sides of the bowl. This is not expected in this day and age. We are in a fine dining setup not some road side stall.

The other issue we faced was that while we were dining the waiter tried to pick up the dips even though we weren't done. He did not even bother asking. I'll put it down to new staff.

But a couple of incidents in a short span of time aren't a good impression.

Service needs improvement even though the food is great.

featured_reviews.name: Sayed Sana Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shameful & Disturbing Incident Outside Mani’s, Mulund (18th Oct 2025)
This review isn’t about food — it’s about basic humanity, which I saw completely missing outside Mani’s, Mulund West on the evening of 18th October 2025 (Saturday) during Diwali time.
While I was having dosa with my family, I witnessed something horrifying — a tall man in a kurta slapped and dragged a young beggar girl right outside the café. She must have been barely 10–12 years old. He hit her so hard, then grabbed her by her t-shirt and pulled her, while everyone just stood there and watched. It was one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen.
And what shocked me most — not one single person from Mani’s staff or management came forward. No one tried to stop that man or even check on that child. Everyone simply ignored it as if nothing happened. Even after assaulting her, that man came back to collect his parcel calmly while his wife sat in the car watching!
I want to ask Mani’s management — do your CCTV cameras not work? Did no staff member see this? Why didn’t anyone step up? It happened right at your doorstep. If you claim to be a family-friendly place, you also have a moral responsibility to protect people outside your premises, especially a child being assaulted in public view.
That moment made me lose all respect for this place. Good food means nothing when basic humanity and courage are missing. I truly hope Mani’s management takes this seriously, checks their CCTV footage from 18th October, identifies that man, and at least reports this inhuman act. Silence in such situations is shameful.

This place in Mumbai is famous for their Authentic Missal Pao, and new varieties of fusion missal pao where they use cheese and other items
. They have seating capacity of around 60 persons. Outlet remain packed as their Missal Pao is delicious.

Service is prompt. Staff is polite. Food is delicious.

They serve coconut chutney with their Missal Pao which enhance the taste.

For those who don't know missal pav features a spicy curry, typically made with sprouted moth beans (matki). The curry, known as "usal," is a delicious blend of aromatic spices, chilies, and herbs that simmer to create a rich and flavorful base. This base is then paired with a thinner, tangy gravy, resulting in a delightful textural contrast.

But wait, there's more! Missal pav isn't just about the curry. A true explosion of flavors comes from the toppings. Chopped onions and cilantro add a refreshing touch, while crunchy farsan (a savory mix of fried gram flour bits) provides a delightful textural contrast. A squeeze of lemon juice adds a zingy pop, and for those who love it hot, a fiery red chili chutney is often offered on the side.
Varieties to Tantalize Your Palate

While the core of missal pav remains the same, there are regional variations that add a unique twist to this beloved dish. Kolhapuri missal, for instance, is known for its fiery heat, while Puneri missal offers a more balanced flavor profile. Some variations even incorporate vegetables like potatoes or tomatoes into the usal.
